verdicts.reason: With pooling and assume_role enabled, the pool configure callback calls compose_sql, which opens a cursor on the owning Django wrapper before its getconn() has returned (postgresql/base.py:231,345-348,369-381; operations.py:192-193; psycopg_any.py:20-22; base/base.py:255-256,270-279), causing recursive pool checkout or cross-thread wrapper use; incidence was not measured.

If the alias pool was opened before test setup, its cached connection parameters retain the original dbname (postgresql/base.py:208,224-241,274-278) when create_test_db closes only the wrapper and changes NAME before migration (base/creation.py:62-83), so test operations can target the original database; incidence was not measured.

If a request changes its session role or time zone and returns its connection, the pool has no reset callback, and later checkouts skip configuration (postgresql/base.py:228-233,345-348,385-405), allowing the next request to inherit those settings; incidence was not measured.

The documented pool option accepts a dict (docs/ref/databases.txt:255-258), but an empty dict causes pool to return None (postgresql/base.py:203-206), so the supported input silently disables pooling; incidence was not measured.
